subject: Biology
title: Chemical Coordination and Integration
summary: Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals that act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts. Endocrine glands are ductless and release hormones into blood.
The hypothalamus controls the pituitary through releasing and inhibiting hormones (adenohypophysis) and by sending oxytocin and vasopressin down axons to the neurohypophysis.
Other glands: pineal, thyroid, parathyroid, thymus, adrenal, pancreas (islets of Langerhans), testes and ovaries. The heart, kidney and gut also make hormones.

Hormones act through receptors: protein hormones bind membrane receptors and use second messengers (cAMP, IP₃, Ca²⁺); steroid and iodothyronine hormones enter the cell and bind intracellular receptors to regulate genes.

formulas.name: Hypothalamic hormones
formulas.formula: GnRH → pituitary makes gonadotrophins;  somatostatin inhibits growth hormone release

formulas.name: Adenohypophysis (pars distalis)
formulas.formula: GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH;  pars intermedia: MSH

formulas.name: Growth hormone disorders
formulas.formula: excess in childhood → gigantism;  deficiency → pituitary dwarfism;  excess in adults → acromegaly (especially of face)

formulas.name: Neurohypophysis
formulas.formula: stores and releases oxytocin (uterine contraction at childbirth, milk ejection) and vasopressin/ADH (water reabsorption in distal tubules; deficiency → diabetes insipidus)
formulas.mistake: These hormones are made in the hypothalamus, not in the posterior pituitary.

formulas.name: Pineal gland
formulas.formula: melatonin → diurnal (24-hour) rhythm of sleep–wake, body temperature; also affects metabolism, pigmentation, menstrual cycle, defence

formulas.name: Thyroid
formulas.formula: T₄ (thyroxine) and T₃ (triiodothyronine) — basal metabolic rate, RBC formation, metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and fats, water and electrolyte balance;  thyrocalcitonin (TCT) lowers blood Ca²⁺

formulas.name: Thyroid disorders
formulas.formula: iodine deficiency → hypothyroidism and goitre;  in pregnancy → cretinism in the baby (stunted growth, mental retardation, deaf-mutism);  hyperthyroidism → exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease: enlarged thyroid, protruding eyes, weight loss)

formulas.name: Parathyroid hormone (PTH)
formulas.formula: raises blood Ca²⁺: bone resorption (demineralisation), Ca²⁺ reabsorption from renal tubules and absorption from digested food;  with TCT maintains Ca²⁺ balance

formulas.name: Thymus
formulas.formula: thymosins → differentiation of T-lymphocytes (cell-mediated immunity) and antibody production (humoral immunity); degenerates with age

formulas.name: Adrenal medulla
formulas.formula: adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline — emergency hormones (fight or flight): alertness, pupil dilation, piloerection, sweating, increased heart rate, breathing rate, glycogenolysis

formulas.name: Adrenal cortex
formulas.formula: zona glomerulosa → mineralocorticoids (aldosterone: Na⁺, water reabsorption, K⁺ and phosphate excretion);  zona fasciculata → glucocorticoids (cortisol: gluconeogenesis, anti-inflammatory, immunosuppression);  zona reticularis → androgens
formulas.note: Underproduction of adrenal cortex hormones causes Addison's disease.

formulas.name: Pancreatic islets
formulas.formula: α-cells → glucagon (hyperglycaemic: glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis);  β-cells → insulin (hypoglycaemic: glucose uptake by cells, glycogenesis);  prolonged hyperglycaemia → diabetes mellitus

formulas.name: Gonads
formulas.formula: testes (Leydig cells) → androgens, mainly testosterone;  ovary → oestrogen (growth of female sex organs, secondary sexual characters) and progesterone (from corpus luteum; supports pregnancy, alveoli of mammary glands)

formulas.name: Hormones of heart, kidney, gut
formulas.formula: heart: ANF (lowers BP);  kidney: erythropoietin (RBC formation);  gut: gastrin, secretin, cholecystokinin (CCK), gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP)

examples.title: Same gland, opposite actions
examples.problem: Which two hormones keep blood calcium constant, and how?
examples.solution: PTH (parathyroid) raises blood Ca²⁺; thyrocalcitonin (thyroid) lowers it. Together they maintain balance.

examples.title: Emergency hormone
examples.problem: Why are adrenaline and noradrenaline called the 3F hormones?
examples.solution: They are released quickly in emergencies — fight, flight or fright — raising heart rate, alertness and blood glucose.

examples.title: Cretinism
examples.problem: A baby shows stunted growth and mental retardation; the mother had iodine deficiency during pregnancy. Diagnosis?
examples.solution: Cretinism — hypothyroidism during pregnancy affects the development of the foetus.

examples.title: Steroid hormone mechanism
examples.problem: How does cortisol act on a target cell?
examples.solution: Being lipid-soluble, it crosses the membrane, binds an intracellular receptor and the hormone–receptor complex regulates gene expression in the nucleus.

examples.title: Second messenger
examples.problem: Name second messengers used by protein hormones.
examples.solution: cAMP, IP₃ and Ca²⁺. The hormone binds a membrane receptor and the second messenger carries the signal inside the cell.

examples.title: Gastrointestinal hormones
examples.problem: Which hormone stimulates pancreatic juice and bile release?
examples.solution: Cholecystokinin (CCK) acts on both pancreas and gall bladder; secretin acts on exocrine pancreas (water and bicarbonate). Gastrin stimulates gastric glands.

topics.title: Endocrine glands and hormones
topics.explain: Classical definition: chemicals made by endocrine glands, released into blood and carried to a distant target organ. Current definition: non-nutrient chemicals that act as intercellular messengers, in trace amounts.

topics.title: Human endocrine system
topics.explain: Pituitary, pineal, thyroid, adrenal, pancreas, parathyroid, thymus and gonads, plus hormone-producing tissues in the gastrointestinal tract, liver, kidney and heart.

topics.title: Hypothalamus
topics.explain: The basal part of the diencephalon; has several groups of neurosecretory cells (nuclei) making hormones that regulate the synthesis and secretion of pituitary hormones. Hormones reach the anterior pituitary through a portal circulatory system.

topics.title: Pituitary gland
topics.explain: Located in the sella turcica (bony cavity), attached to the hypothalamus by a stalk. Anatomically adenohypophysis (pars distalis, pars intermedia) and neurohypophysis (pars nervosa).

topics.title: Chemical nature of hormones
topics.explain: Peptide/polypeptide/protein (insulin, glucagon, pituitary and hypothalamic hormones), steroids (cortisol, testosterone, oestradiol, progesterone), iodothyronines (thyroid hormones), amino acid derivatives (adrenaline, noradrenaline, epinephrine).

topics.title: Mechanism of hormone action
topics.explain: Hormones bind specific receptors on target tissues only. Membrane-bound receptors (for those that can't enter) form a hormone–receptor complex that generates second messengers; intracellular receptors (mostly nuclear) regulate gene expression or chromosome function.

ratta: Anterior pituitary: GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH;  intermediate: MSH.
Oxytocin & ADH made in hypothalamus, released from posterior pituitary.
GH excess: child gigantism, adult acromegaly.
Glomerulosa → aldosterone;  fasciculata → cortisol;  reticularis → androgens.
Graves = hyperthyroid;  cretinism = hypothyroid in pregnancy;  Addison = low corticoids.
